title: Steven Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC denied Hahn’s appeal from his guilty judgment on all three charges, leaving undisturbed the censure of indefinite suspension from the sacraments.
first_summary: Hahn appealed Presbytery’s guilty verdict and indefinite suspension from the sacraments, alleging trial irregularities, haste, prejudice, and improper refusal of an amendment. The SJC upheld all three convictions. Applying BCO 39-3.3, it deferred to Presbytery’s familiarity with the parties, witnesses, and lengthy trial record and concluded that contrary evidence did not establish clear error.
summary: Hahn appealed Presbytery’s guilty judgment and indefinite suspension from the sacraments, alleging trial irregularities, denial of a requested amendment, haste, and prejudice. The SJC denied the appeal on all three charges: false and unsubstantiated accusations, disobedience and disrespect toward church authorities, and a bitter and malignant spirit. Applying BCO 39-3.3, it deferred to Presbytery’s familiarity with the parties, witnesses, and extensive trial record and found no clear error, even though contrary evidence may have existed. The judgment and censure therefore remained undisturbed.
